newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's Autoliv, ATI to form 'smart airbags' joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's Autoliv, ATI to form 'smart airbags' joint venture.

text.p: Sweden's Autoliv said Monday it would form a jointly owned company with Automotive Technologies International Inc. of Detroit to develop and produce ATI's patented ultrasound sensor for car airbags.
"The system is planned to be used in the self-adjusting airbag system which Autoliv is now developing," Autoliv said in a statment.
"The new jointly owned company, Autoliv-ATI, will have global rights to ATI's ultrasound sensors and several complementary products," Autoliv said.
A final contract is expected within a month, it said.

The self-adjusting, or smart airbags, are said to prevent injury caused by ordinary airbags because they are able to sense if there is a reverse facing child safety seat in the front seat or if there is a passenger sitting near the dashboard.
ATI was started in 1988 by David Breed, who also founded of Breed Technologies, Inc. ATI has more than 40 patents for various collision sensors and intelligent airbag systems, Autoliv said.
